podcast.body: Adele's "Rolling in the Deep" was the second best-selling digital track of the 2010s, selling 8.9 million copies. Its strong digital performance highlighted Adele's popularity and ability to drive sales in a period of transition for music consumption. "They were followed by Adele's Rolling in the Deep with sales of 8.9 million."

podcast.body: This song stood out from her album "21," being described as "aching, but defiant, soulful, but a banging." In a year dominated by EDM club pop, this thumping torch song sounded at home in a club but was bigger than the club. Rolling Stone magazine ranked it as "the year's biggest hit" and "its most visionary." It commanded 2011, similar to how The Beatles commanded 1964. "In a year, a wash in EDM club pop, songs that made the year end top five included LMFAO's party rock anthem and pit bulls give me everything. Adele's thumping torch song sounded at home in a club, but bigger than the club."

podcast.body: This song was Adele's signature torch song of the 2010s, which hit number one. Aretha Franklin covered it in 2014, titling her version "Rolling in the Deep, The Aritha Version." "Adels rolling in the deep. Franklin covered it in 2014, just three years after Adels' original hit number 1."
